## Specific task description

Task instruction: Grasp the compact tea box and the small scanner fits in hand simultaneously using separate arms, then scan.

Task description: Use separate arms to hold the black handheld scanner left of center and green-yellow tea box on the right. While holding both, bring the scanning end close and face it toward the tea box to scan.

Success criteria: The tea box must align near the outward scanning axis and lie within a short scanning range directly in front of the scanning end. Separate arms must simultaneously hold the scanner and tea box, with both grippers closed.

## Execution tips

- Grasp the scanner's narrower middle handle across opposing sides, opening slightly wider than that section. Avoid the broad scan head and leave room to orient its scanning end toward the tea box.
- Grip areas of two opposite tea-box faces away from corners, fully seating the pads and leaving the scanner-approach side clear. This avoids box rotation from corner grasps or obstruction of the scanning end by the gripper.
- Before closing, use a side view if possible to confirm both fingers enclose the grasp section. Pay particular attention to the tabletop clearance below the scanner handle so the fingertips do not press against the table or merely push the object.
- Adjust relative orientation away from the table with surrounding clearance. During close alignment, hold one object steady and make small position and orientation adjustments to the other, avoiding a backward scanner, missing the tea box sideways or colliding grippers.
